$ outreach --help
--- stdout
usage: outreach [-h]
                {send,tick,postmaster,resume,inbox,replies,reply,build,pressed,suppress,status,assets,ai-test,warmup,approve,probe,doctor} ...

outreach — the email lane: the one outbound channel the machine runs end to end
(ROADMAP B46, plan ~/projects/plans/20-email-lane.md, GROWTH § 5.3 / § 5.5 / § 8.1).

  outreach send [--go] [--dry-run] [--only 1 3] [--hold 2] [--touch 0|3|10]
                               # the day's approved emails: reads `leads kit --remote --json`,
                               # skips no-address and suppressed picks, renders the approved
                               # letter, sends, logs the pipeline through `leads`, one ledger row
  outreach send --batch FILE|- [--dry-run | --go]
                               # B90: a batch from `leads batch --json` (plan 37 § Contract).
                               # --dry-run renders every first letter; no flag lists the names
                               # and their two faults for Taylor's `go`; --go queues three
                               # touches a business (day 0, 3, 10, never a fourth) and runs a tick
  outreach tick                # sends what is due now: one letter a mailbox a tick at most,
                               # irregular gaps across working hours, under each mailbox's cap
  outreach postmaster 0.08 [--domain D]   # record a Google Postmaster spam-rate reading (percent)
  outreach postmaster fetch|check|grant   # B136: the reading by API, daily (lib/postmaster.py)
  outreach resume MAILBOX | --lane        # Taylor's word after a pause or a stop
  outreach inbox [--dry-run]   # replies since the cursor: classified, the routine ones answered,
                               # the warm ones handed to Taylor with a brief
  outreach replies [--open|--today|--since D|NAME] [--json|--count]
                               # B105: every reply thread across the three mailboxes, newest first:
                               # who, which mailbox, the letter they got, what they said, the class,
                               # and whether the machine answered, Taylor did, or it waits on him
  outreach reply NAME "words" [--any]   # B105: Taylor's own words in that thread, from its mailbox,
                               # with his name, phone and the postal address; no template, no AI
  outreach build [NAME]        # B92, Taylor's word after an interested reply: `prep one` for that
                               # business, detached; the outline comes by notify. Nothing else starts it
  outreach suppress add hello@x.example | ChIJ…      # off the list for good, both channels
  outreach pressed PLACE_ID [--url U]       # B91: a press on the see link stops its touches, offers build
  outreach suppress ls [--json]            # --json: [{value, kind: address|domain|place_id}] for `leads batch`
  outreach status              # today's sends, the caps, replies by class, bounces, complaints
  outreach status --by variant|fault|segment|letter|prebuilt
                               # B132: per group, one business once: delivered → preview clicks →
                               # replies → positive replies → customers, each per hundred delivered,
                               # and "too few to decide" below the floor (100 a group, 20 positive)
  outreach status --by arm      # B137: the close test (E3), Taylor's call vs Patch's link: interested,
                               # Patch answered, claimed, paid, each per hundred interested
  outreach status --by experiment E1
                               # B142: a registered experiment (the venture's experiments.json): the seven
                               # stages per arm counted by business, "too few to decide" under the floor, the
                               # stages past its primary endpoint bracketed and split by the next one's arm
  outreach status --by actor|channel|provider|asset|strength
                               # B142: the seven stages by a whole-population dimension; any other cut, or
                               # two experiments crossed, is refused with the reason
  outreach ai-test start | stop [--keep intro|foot|none] | show
                               # B132, plan 53: the AI-line test. Open, each batch is dealt a third each
                               # to none / intro / foot; start and stop are Taylor's word only, as `go` is
  outreach warmup [start DATE] # the warm-up state and the ramp; `start` records the day warm-up began
  outreach assets [--json|--check]   # B141: the capacity registry, mailbox -> domain -> tenant -> provider,
                               # each row's state, caps, counts and the contract verdict; --check exits 1
                               # on a broken rule (the evening check). `assets state NAME STATE --why "…"`,
                               # `assets incident NAME "…"`, `assets set NAME --cap N --verdict V …` change one
  outreach approve             # Taylor's one command after reading templates/outreach/*.md
  outreach doctor              # keys by name, the address, the template, the caps, the provider

Why email and nothing else: CAN-SPAM has no B2B exception but permits a truthful,
addressed, opt-out-honouring note, and it is the only cold channel where the
machine may send, read the reply, answer and hand over (GROWTH § 8.1). A cold text
or an AI voice call never becomes legal, so nothing here ever texts or dials.

What every email carries (GROWTH § 5.3, checked, not promised): who Taylor is and
where, the one fault from the pick's own listing, the preview link, Starter's exact
price sentence if they want it kept, the phone and the booking link, the postal
address, a plain line saying it is an advertisement from a local business, "reply
'no thanks' and you won't hear from me again", and the one-line disclosure Taylor
decided: Patch found it and drafted it, Taylor reads every one before it goes.

The letters live in templates/outreach/ and Taylor approves their exact text once:
APPROVED holds a sha256 per template and `send` refuses while one is missing or
stale, so editing a letter un-approves it; the hash covers the price sentences a
letter carries too (lib/prices.py), so a new price un-approves it the same way. The subjects come from the same file.
`outreach doctor` renders a sample of each and checks the rules (four to six
sentences, one link in the letter — the preview; the booking link, the phone and
the address sit in the signature, which is not the pitch — the ad identification,
the opt-out, the disclosure, and no money in a cold letter that isn't
`{price_line}`). The one exception is `{paying}` (B71): a sentence `leads` builds from
client-leads/vendor_prices.md in the *vendor's* published or reported price ("Your site's
address is set up with Hibu, whose plans are reported to start at $449 a month."), never a
guess at the lead's bill; it is empty — and the sentence gone — when the vendor is unknown.

Two weeks of `go`: `send` does nothing without `--go` unless OUTREACH_AUTO=1 (the
schedule passes `--go` on the morning Taylor replied `go`). Everything money- or
volume-shaped is an environment number, never a sentence in a prompt:

  OUTREACH_PER_DAY             sends a day. Default 0 — out of the box this tool
                               sends nothing at all.
  OUTREACH_MAX_REPLIES_PER_DAY machine replies a day (default 10); never more than
                               one machine reply per thread per day, ever.
  OUTREACH_AI_USD_PER_DAY      the classifier's daily spend (default 0.50); over it,
                               nothing is machine-answered and everything unclear
                               goes to Taylor.
  OUTREACH_BOUNCE_MAX_PCT      the kill switch (default 2.0, Taylor 2026-10-01). Over it, or any spam
                               complaint, `send` refuses, Taylor is notified and one
                               TAYLOR-TODO §7 entry is filed.
  OUTREACH_COMPLAINTS          complaints seen in Google Postmaster Tools (Instantly
                               reports no complaint count of its own). Any value
                               above zero trips the switch.
  OUTREACH_AUTO                1 = the two weeks of `go` are over (the kit lane only: a batch
                               always waits on `go`, because its letter says "I approve each batch").
  OUTREACH_PREVIEW_DAYS        how long a preview stands (default 14); the day-10
                               letter names the date it comes down.

Config, by name, never printed:
  INSTANTLY_API_KEY       ~/.config/claude-tools/env. Never Resend (its terms forbid
                          cold mail) and never patchlamp.com's domain — a burned
                          domain would take the product's mail with it.
  ANTHROPIC_KEY_OUTREACH  the classifier's key, falling back to ANTHROPIC_KEY_RELAY.
  OUTREACH_FROM           the outreach mailbox (Instantly's `eaccount`).
  OUTREACH_PROVIDER       instantly | fake. Default: instantly once the key is set,
                          else fake. `--dry-run` never touches the network.
  LEADS_MAIL_ADDRESS      the postal address every commercial email must carry.
                          Required: without it nothing sends, as in `leads`.
  LEADS_BOOKING_URL       the booking link (Cal.com).
  PATCHLAMP_VOICE_NUMBER  the phone line; without it the phone line is dropped.
  PATCHLAMP_DEMO_NUMBER   the demo number people text themselves (default
                          435-901-7141).
  OUTREACH_STATE          state dir (default ~/.local/state/claude-tools/outreach)
  OUTREACH_TEMPLATES      the letters (default ../templates/outreach beside this file)
  INSTANTLY_API_BASE / ANTHROPIC_API_BASE    tests only: stand-ins for the real hosts.
  OUTREACH_LEADS_BIN / OUTREACH_NOTIFY_BIN / OUTREACH_PREP_BIN
                          tests only: stand-ins for `leads` / `notify` / `prep`.
  OUTREACH_KIT_JSON       tests only: a kit file instead of running `leads`.

The provider is an interface with two implementations. `fake` keeps everything in
files under the state dir and is what the tests and `--dry-run` use. `instantly` is
Instantly's API v2 (see the plan's § Contract for every endpoint). Instantly has no
single-send endpoint on any plan — `/emails/send-test` never enters the Unibox and
`/emails/reply` only replies — so a send is a campaign plus a lead: one campaign
whose step is `{{subject_line}}` / `{{body_html}}`, and each pick a lead carrying
its own rendered letter. Every sentence is therefore composed here, where the
template checks run; Instantly is only the transport and the warm-up.

Money: a send costs nothing of ours (the mailbox is a flat monthly bill), so its
ledger row carries cost 0 and exists to count sends. Each classifier call is its own
row with its real cost. Both land in ~/.local/state/claude-tools/ledger.jsonl.

The pipeline is never written here: every conversation goes in through `leads log`
and `leads sent`, so one tool owns that file.

---- The batch lane (B90, plan ~/projects/plans/37-email-at-volume.md) ----------------

Batches of up to fifty researched businesses from `leads batch --json`, each with an
address and exactly two fault sentences. Taylor's `go` approves a batch (the names and
their faults, `outreach send --batch FILE` without --go prints exactly that); --go
queues three touches a business in state/sequences.json and the tick sends them. The
letters are templates/outreach/batch-{first,second,third}.md, approved like the others:
the first carries the two faults verbatim and no link at all (a reply is the
conversation we want, and filters score every domain inside a cold first message); the
second and third may carry one link, and only on the sending domain
(OUTREACH_LINK_BASE), else they ask for a reply too. No letter says a site was built
unless that business has a preview URL: `send` refuses such a letter in code.

The `google` provider sends through each mailbox's own Google mail server (SMTP) and
reads replies there (IMAP), because Instantly's Growth plan, which warms the mailboxes,
has no API. Instantly's warm-up network writes into the same inboxes all day, so a
message is a reply only if its In-Reply-To/References name a Message-ID we sent, or,
failing that, it comes from an address we wrote to; everything else is never read as a
reply, classified or answered. A reply of any kind but an automatic one stops that
business's remaining touches. Delivery-status reports are counted per mailbox and per
batch. Follow-ups go from the same mailbox in the same thread.

Pacing, because bursts at fixed intervals are what a filter reads as a machine: one
letter per mailbox per tick at most, the gap to the next drawn at random around the
time left in the window divided by the letters left, never under
OUTREACH_MIN_GAP_MINUTES, weekdays inside OUTREACH_SEND_HOURS only. Follow-ups go
before new first letters and count toward the same cap.

  OUTREACH_MAILBOXES           the Workspace entry's addresses, comma-separated. Since B150 the lane's
                               mailboxes are the registry's (`outreach assets`): a first letter goes only
                               through an `active` one under a PERMITTED contract, half per contract at most,
                               and a follow-up from its thread's own mailbox; a Factory mailbox joins on
                               `infra certify` and leaves on `infra drain`, with no env edit
                               (e.g. taylor@trypatchlamp.com,t.remund@trypatchlamp.com,...)
  OUTREACH_APP_PASSWORD_<ADDR> one Google app password per mailbox, the address upper-cased
                               with every other character an underscore:
                               OUTREACH_APP_PASSWORD_TAYLOR_TRYPATCHLAMP_COM
  OUTREACH_MAILBOX_PER_DAY     each mailbox's daily cap. A number, or a ramp by days since
                               the warm-up start: "14:5,21:20,28:28" = nothing before day 14,
                               5 a day from day 14, 20 from day 21, 28 from day 28. Default 0:
                               nothing sends. Follow-ups count toward it.
  OUTREACH_WARMUP_START        YYYY-MM-DD the warm-up began (or `outreach warmup start DATE`,
                               kept in the state dir; the env wins)
  OUTREACH_SEND_HOURS          the sending window, Taylor's clock (default 8-17), weekdays only
  OUTREACH_MIN_GAP_MINUTES     the least time between two letters from one mailbox (default 6)
  OUTREACH_FROM_NAME           the From name (default "Taylor Remund")
  OUTREACH_LINK_BASE           the second touch's link base, on the sending domain only
                               (e.g. https://see.trypatchlamp.com); unset = ask for a reply
  OUTREACH_SMTP_HOST / OUTREACH_IMAP_HOST   default smtp.gmail.com:465 / imap.gmail.com:993
                               (tests point them at loopback servers)
  OUTREACH_VERIFY              none | millionverifier. Every first send is checked first.
                               With none, the first 30 days after the warm-up start send only
                               to addresses the batch marks MX-ok on the business's own domain.
  MILLIONVERIFIER_API_KEY      the verifier's key (about $0.004 an address); one ledger row a
                               check. OUTREACH_VERIFY_BASE is a test stand-in for its host.
  OUTREACH_NOW                 tests only: the clock (ISO time, Taylor's zone if naive).

The stop rules (Taylor, 2026-10-01, answer 2): one angry or "this is spam" reply pauses
that mailbox and tells Taylor; the lane stops when angry replies plus unsubscribes exceed
OUTREACH_ANGRY_MAX_PCT (1.0) of the last OUTREACH_COMPLAINT_WINDOW (1,000) sends (the
window counts as 1,000 until there are 1,000, so one polite "no thanks" among the first
fifty can't stop a lane), when bounces exceed OUTREACH_BOUNCE_MAX_PCT (2.0) per mailbox or
per batch (over at least OUTREACH_BOUNCE_MIN_SENDS, 50, sends), or when a recorded
Postmaster spam rate is at or above OUTREACH_SPAM_RATE_MAX_PCT (0.1). A stop files a
TAYLOR-TODO §7 entry and holds until `outreach resume --lane`; counting starts afresh then.

positional arguments:
  {send,tick,postmaster,resume,inbox,replies,reply,build,pressed,suppress,status,assets,ai-test,warmup,approve,probe,doctor}
    send                the day's approved emails
    tick                send what is due now (the timer runs it)
    postmaster          record a Postmaster spam-rate reading (percent)
    resume              a paused mailbox, or the stopped lane, back on
    inbox               replies: classified, the routine ones answered
    replies             B105: every reply thread across the mailboxes, newest
                        first (last 14 days)
    reply               B105: Taylor's own words, in the thread, from the
                        mailbox that owns it
    build               Taylor's `build`: the researched site (prep one) for
                        an interested reply
    pressed             B91: a business pressed its letter's link; stop its
                        touches, offer `build` (one JSON object)
    suppress            off the list for good
    status              today's sends, the caps, the replies, the bounce rate
    assets              B141: the capacity registry — mailbox, domain, tenant,
                        provider
    ai-test             B132: the AI-line test — start | stop [--keep V] |
                        show (start and stop on Taylor's word only)
    warmup              the warm-up state and the ramp
    approve             print each letter, then record Taylor's approval
    probe               one plain test mail from each mailbox to an address
                        (Taylor's ask)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
--- stderr
--- exit 0
